summary: This short program creates three Room objects using the Room class's no-argument constructor and prints each one. It shows that every `new` gives you a separate object, and that printing an object calls its toString() method.

lines.text: A separate application class whose only job is to exercise the Room domain class; keeping the data class and the program that uses it apart is normal Java practice.
The entry point the Java launcher calls when you run RoomDesign.
Calls Room's no-argument constructor, which builds a room with its default field values, and stores a reference to that new object in room1.
A second, completely independent Room object; changing one room later would not affect the other.
A simple heading so the output that follows is easy to read.
Passing an object to println invokes its toString() method, so what you see here is whatever description the Room class defines.
